decision: Model every native-values closed-set parameter as str in compiler/internal/catalogue/catalogue.json and enforce membership in the new NT-I01 checker admission module: mirror the four authoritative TS tables (NATIVE_MAKE_KINDS 4, NATIVE_OBSERVE_KINDS 7, NATIVE_HOSTILE_DESCRIPTORS 3, NATIVE_READ_OPS 5), require string literals for closed-set arguments, and reject non-member literals, following the checkBrowserTag precedent in compiler/internal/check/browser.go. The 7 sets without tables stay plain str with review-enforced membership documented. Mirror the 7-member observe const; file the 9-member note as a K-lane finding. Drop the proposal nativeTest block (DisallowUnknownFields).

disagreements.note: Response 1 is a near-split: str_with_checker_allowlist 0.60 vs variant_unit_leaves 0.37. The variant reading is attractive because the type checker alone would reject unlisted members with no literal inspection. Investigated and set aside: it costs 19 new leaf types plus 19 emitter lowerings against one checker module with exact in-tree precedent (checkBrowserTag), and leaf-per-member lockstep with the TS tables is a larger unreviewable surface than a mirrored allowlist. Responses 2 and 3 agree with the allowlist at 0.78 and 0.91.

interpretation: Three fresh phrasings unanimously favor str_with_checker_allowlist (0.60, 0.78, 0.91). Agreement is advisory only; the choice is independently supported by the exact checkBrowserTag precedent for static string-literal validation in compiler/internal/check/browser.go, the catalogue's lack of an enum kind, and the lockstep-cost argument against 19 leaf types or 19 constructors. It does not prove correctness or remove bias, and authorizes no execution or qualification.
